purpose: Conservative, provisional campus few-shot enrollment selected after independent visual review and root high-resolution audit.
privacy_note: This manifest contains relative filenames, labels, review evidence, source URLs, and the archive checksum only. It intentionally contains no absolute paths, GPS coordinates, or EXIF metadata.
model_status: provisional enrollment only; no production approval, deployment promotion, or safety-gate changes.
identification_method: Visual review of all three-view runs, duplicate-aware grouping, authoritative taxonomy/trait cross-checks, and a root high-resolution audit. Exact cultivar resolution is not asserted where photographs do not support it.

hashing.archive_sha256: SHA-256 above identifies the operator-supplied archive.
hashing.image_sha256: The per-file SHA-256 map below lets preparation verify every archive image before materializing the accepted subset; the generated artifact records the accepted hashes again for runtime provenance.

accepted_classes.label: Alpinia zerumbet 'Variegata'
accepted_classes.evidence: Broad lanceolate leaves with strong cream longitudinal striping, upright clumping ginger habit, and shell-ginger inflorescence.
alternatives: Another variegated Alpinia cultivar; cultivar name is horticultural rather than taxonomic.

accepted_classes.label: Sanchezia oblonga
accepted_classes.evidence: Yellow/cream-veined ornamental shrub foliage in the first reticulate-vein run; root audit separated it from the flowering Pseuderanthemum run.
alternatives: Sanchezia speciosa (synonym); Sanchezia nobilis horticultural usage.

accepted_classes.label: Pseuderanthemum maculatum
accepted_classes.evidence: Yellow/cream reticulate venation plus white flowers with purple/magenta throat spots in the later flowering run.
alternatives: Pseuderanthemum carruthersii horticultural complex; P. reticulatum is a synonym under current Kew treatment.

accepted_classes.label: Chrysalidocarpus lutescens
accepted_classes.evidence: Dense multi-stemmed clump with yellow-green cane-like stems and gracefully arching pinnate fronds.
alternatives: Other clustering areca-type palm; Dypsis lutescens is a former synonym.

accepted_classes.label: Ixora coccinea
accepted_classes.evidence: Glossy opposite elliptic leaves and dense compact clusters of four-lobed red or pink star flowers; two color forms are retained under one species label.
alternatives: Ixora hybrid or another cultivated Ixora species; cultivar/color identity is not asserted.

accepted_classes.label: Serissa japonica
accepted_classes.common_name: Snowrose / tree of a thousand stars
accepted_classes.evidence: Low clipped shrub with very small opposite leaves and numerous small solitary or clustered white pinwheel-like flowers.
alternatives: Wrightia antidysenterica; gardenia or another small-leaved white-flowering hedge.

accepted_classes.label: Tradescantia pallida 'Purpurea'
accepted_classes.evidence: Trailing fleshy stems with narrow lanceolate leaves that are uniformly purple/burgundy.
alternatives: Other purple Tradescantia cultivar; Setcreasea pallida is a synonym.

accepted_classes.label: Duranta erecta
accepted_classes.evidence: Clipped hedge with small opposite leaves, chartreuse/golden new growth, and Duranta-like axillary/terminal flower racemes.
alternatives: Duranta erecta 'Gold Mound', 'Alba', or another yellow-leaved cultivar; cultivar is not asserted.

accepted_classes.label: Tecomaria capensis
accepted_classes.evidence: Orange tubular flowers on a many-stemmed shrub/climber with pinnate, serrated leaflets.
alternatives: Tecoma stans or another Bignoniaceae ornamental; the second yellow-flowered run is kept separate.

accepted_classes.label: Sphagneticola trilobata
accepted_classes.evidence: Trailing groundcover with yellow daisy heads and opposite toothed to variably three-lobed leaves.
alternatives: Sphagneticola calendulacea (Wedelia chinensis), especially where lobing is weak.

accepted_classes.label: Mimusops elengi
accepted_classes.evidence: The sign in IMG_20260905_164101098_HDR.jpg explicitly identifies Mimusops elengi; narrow glossy leaves agree. Only this sign-confirmed run is enrolled.
alternatives: Another Mimusops or unrelated narrow-leaved ornamental cannot be ruled out for unsigned views.

accepted_classes.label: Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis
accepted_classes.evidence: Ornamental double red hibiscus flowers with glossy serrated leaves; cultivar-level identity is not asserted.
alternatives: Other cultivated Hibiscus hybrid, including H. schizopetalus hybrids.

accepted_classes.label: Tecoma stans
accepted_classes.evidence: Root audit resolved this separate yellow-flowered run as Tecoma stans: opposite pinnate leaves with toothed leaflets and yellow trumpet flowers.
alternatives: Tecomaria capensis; Tecoma cultivar. It remains a separate class from the orange Cape honeysuckle run.

accepted_classes.label: Combretum indicum
accepted_classes.evidence: Woody climber with opposite leaves and flowers changing white to pink to red, with long tubular buds.
alternatives: Quisqualis indica is the common former name.

accepted_classes.label: Cordia sebestena
accepted_classes.evidence: Root audit and NParks spot characters match large rough alternate ovate leaves and wrinkled orange funnel flowers in terminal clusters.
alternatives: Cordia subcordata or another Cordia; flower/leaf combination strongly favors C. sebestena.

accepted_classes.label: Caladium horticultural group
accepted_classes.evidence: Peltate heart-shaped leaves emerging from a tuberous clump with strong dark-green reticulate venation; one overexposed view is excluded.
alternatives: Caladium hybrid; Colocasia/Xanthosoma are less consistent with the observed cultivated leaf form.

accepted_classes.label: Heptapleurum arboricola
accepted_classes.evidence: Palmately compound leaflets in potted shrubs; one run has yellow-centered variegation and the other white margins. Species is shared; cultivar is not.
alternatives: Schefflera arboricola is the widespread former name; juvenile H. actinophyllum is less likely.

accepted_classes.label: Cordyline fruticosa
accepted_classes.evidence: Burgundy strap-like leaves arranged in rosettes on red/purple stems or canes.
alternatives: Dracaena reflexa or another Cordyline cultivar; Cordyline terminalis is a horticultural synonym.

accepted_classes.label: Zingiber spectabile
accepted_classes.evidence: Ginger foliage with distinctive tan/brown honeycomb cone-shaped inflorescences.
alternatives: Zingiber zerumbet (shampoo ginger); cone form favors Z. spectabile.

accepted_classes.label: Dracaena trifasciata
accepted_classes.evidence: Upright rigid sword leaves with gray-green mottling and banding.
alternatives: Sansevieria trifasciata is the former horticultural name.

accepted_classes.label: Hymenocallis littoralis
accepted_classes.evidence: Basal strap-leaf clump with white spider-like flowers, long recurved tepals, and a conspicuous central staminal cup.
alternatives: Crinum asiaticum or another Hymenocallis; central cup and flower architecture favor H. littoralis.

accepted_classes.label: Plumeria rubra
accepted_classes.evidence: Pink/magenta five-petaled flowers with long leathery pointed leaves and frangipani branch structure.
alternatives: Plumeria obtusa; leaf apex and flower color favor P. rubra.
